section_summary: This section comprises official diplomatic and interdepartmental correspondence from May to October 1939 regarding reciprocal Federal income tax exemptions for non-diplomatic Japanese government officials stationed in or visiting the United States. Under Section 116(h) of the Internal Revenue Code, the State Department certified to the Treasury Department that Japan granted equivalent tax exemptions to American officials, facilitating tax clearance and sailing permits for Japanese naval inspectors, language officers, academic researchers, and exposition commissioners. The records consist of notes between the Japanese Embassy and the State Department, executive correspondence between State and Treasury, and naval intelligence communications regarding Japanese personnel movements.

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests income tax exemption and departure facilitation for Sakae Yagi, who postponed his sailing and will depart New York for Europe.
subfiles.summary: Japanese Note No. 103: Sakae Yagi postponed his San Francisco departure and will sail from New York May 20, 1939 on the Columbus; asks exemption steps.
subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy Note No. 103 regarding Sakae Yagi's Departure and Tax Exemption

subfiles.about: Assistant Secretary Messersmith transmits the Japanese Ambassador's note concerning Sakae Yagi's rescheduled sailing on the Columbus to the Secretary of the Treasury.
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.to: Henry Morgenthau, Jr., Secretary of the Treasury

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State acknowledges note no. 103 regarding Sakae Yagi's revised travel plans and tax-exempt status.
subfiles.summary: State acknowledges Note No. 103 on Yagi's departure on the Columbus and says a copy went to Treasury.

subfiles.about: The Japanese Ambassador requests tax exemption for landscape architect Nagao Sakurai prior to his departure on the Queen Mary.
